6 A shuttle disk, through Semantic Unison

A shuttle disk carries new photographs from a laptop to the archive. Semantic Unison synchronizes it with the archive’s tree. When only metadata changed, it sends the XMP packet, not the image, and checks with the preserved digest that nothing else moved. Before the shuttle is emptied, Unison preserves what it brought into a DNG Compare archive with the same layout, so a refilled path later gets a new version rather than overwriting the old one. dngc versions lists them and dngc restore --version rebuilds any of them. On either replica, Unison can also keep the last few versions of each file it replaces as skeleton versions, a few kilobytes for the first and a few hundred bytes for each one after, which unison-skeleton lists and restores.

A library that only grows. The same comparison keeps a long-term library as it is while new photographs keep arriving on another disk. unison SOURCE LIBRARY -semdiff looks for every source file in the library and copies only those with no copy there; it never updates or deletes anything in the library. Given a phindex index of each tree (-semindex, once per index), it settles the pairs whose index rows are current without reading either file, and finds a file that was renamed, or renamed and edited, by its content. A photograph that reached the library by another route is found in its index and is not copied twice.
